findings.title: Changing buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks in-flight buffers
findings.body: These `span-buf:s:*` keys previously contained Redis sets, and their TTL allows them to survive for up to an hour. `ZADD` against an existing set fails with `WRONGTYPE`; during a rolling deploy, old workers also fail when they use set commands against keys created as sorted sets by new workers. Batches touching these traces will fail instead of being processed until the old keys expire or the workers are coordinated. Use a versioned key namespace or an explicit migration/drain strategy.

findings.title: Merging overlapping sorted sets changes span eviction scores
findings.body: Redis `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same payload is present in both the canonical set and `parent_key`—for example, a replay recreates the payload under a parent ID that now redirects to the canonical set—the merged member's score becomes the sum of both timestamps rather than its end timestamp. Since the score determines which spans `ZPOPMIN` evicts, repeated deliveries can make old spans look newest and cause genuinely newer spans to be evicted. Preserve a single event score when merging, such as with an appropriate aggregate.

findings.title: Optimized pagination fails for datetime ordering
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation assumes the ordering field is numeric and calls `math.floor` or `math.ceil` on it. On a nonempty first page, cursor construction invokes this method with a `datetime`, raising `TypeError` and making requests with optimized pagination enabled return a server error. The paginator needs datetime-aware cursor key and value handling, or the endpoint must use a compatible paginator.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to unsupported Django queryset slicing
findings.body: This branch deliberately evaluates `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django querysets reject negative slice indices and raise `ValueError` when evaluated; they do not handle negative offsets as the comment claims. A request using an advanced cursor with a negative offset therefore fails instead of paginating.

findings.title: The configured maximum segment span count is no longer honored
findings.body: The Lua script now always caps sets at 1000, while `SpansBuffer` still exposes `max_segment_spans` as a constructor option. The previous load-time check enforcing that option was removed, so a buffer configured with a lower limit can now retain and return more spans than its configured bound; a higher limit is also silently capped at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the script or retain enforcement of the option.
